subject: Risk-based evidence roadmap & FedRAMP/ISO sequencing
messages:
From: Sally Park <sally.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence ask + sequencing question for FedRAMP/ISO

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the team at Acme is excited about Redwood's routing/fallback approach. As we start scoping our procurement and security intake, the security team asked for a prioritized list of evidence you can provide for SOC 2, SIG, and CAIQ, and a short plan for ISO 27001 / FedRAMP sequencing.

Two specific asks:
- Can you share an evidence matrix (owner + earliest delivery date) for SOC 2 in the next 30 days?
- For FedRAMP readiness: do you have a risk-based sequencing plan (which controls we'll address first, and whether you expect any control gaps requiring compensating controls)?

We're trying to create a realistic timeline for our auditors — any high-level guidance on what typically takes longer would help.

Thanks,
Sally Park
Director, InfoSec - Acme Corp

Attachment: sample-acme-integration-scope.pdf (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence ask + sequencing question for FedRAMP/ISO

Hi Sally — great to hear, and appreciate the clarity on asks.

High level responses:
1) Evidence matrix: we have an internal SOC 2 evidence spreadsheet we can share off-cycle; I'll attach a cleaned export with owners and earliest delivery windows. Expect most config / policy evidence within 10–14 business days (policies, role definitions, IAM configs), but sampling artifacts (logs, retention proofs) may need 30–45 business days depending on retention windows.

2) FedRAMP sequencing: we recommend a risk-first approach — prioritize identity/access controls, logging & monitoring, and data-in-transit/storage encryption. Those typically unblock auditor scope and mitigate the largest gaps. Some controls (e.g., continuous monitoring and incident response readiness) are iterative; you should assume staged evidence delivery. If there are specific control gaps that map to third-party dependencies, we will flag them and propose compensating controls.

I'll drop a short evidence roadmap and attach a preliminary SOC2-evidence-matrix_v1.xlsx and a fedramp-gap-scan-summary.pdf. Marissa, can you add estimated delivery dates for the items you own? Mina — can you confirm whether the retention artifacts can be exported earlier than the stated retention window?

Next steps:
- We will send the matrix today, call out high-risk controls, and propose a 6-8 week phased delivery plan.
- If Acme wants an accelerated window (e.g., for a Q4 procurement deadline), we'll surface extra resource needs and where we can commit accelerators.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-matrix_v1.xlsx, fedramp-gap-scan-summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sally Park <sally.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence ask + sequencing question for FedRAMP/ISO

Thanks Karthik — I filled in owner ETA estimates in the matrix for the items I own (see "owner_notes" column). Quick clarifications for Acme:
- "IAM config export" refers to exported role-to-policy bindings from our IAM console (we can provide CSV + a filtered IAM snapshot).
- "Key management evidence" will show our KMS integration (config screenshots + policy doc); hardware-backed keys (HSM) are part of Private deployments — let me know if you need HSM attestation or KMS audit logs.

Mina: I flagged a retention artifact (S3 lifecycle logs) that may be truncated if we pull earlier than the retention window — note in the matrix where sampling artifacts will require waiting for a complete window.

Sally: if you can indicate which auditor (or FedRAMP path: MODERATE / HIGH) you plan to pursue, we can tailor the sequencing and note any additional evidentiary requirements.

-Marissa

Attachment referenced: SOC2-evidence-matrix_v1.xlsx (updated owner ETA)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sally Park <sally.park@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence ask + sequencing question for FedRAMP/ISO

Sally — quick note on retention artifacts: for a few controls we only have rolling 90-day logs in the hot path and archived logs beyond that. If Acme's auditors want a 12-month sampling window, we'll need to pull from cold archives which may add 5–7 business days for extraction and redaction. For expedited timelines we can provide sampled windows + attestations of retention configuration earlier.

Also: for ISO 27001, our typical timeline when started in parallel with SOC 2 is ~4–6 months to reach documentation completeness and internal audit readiness (assuming resource allocation for policy gaps and control remediations). FedRAMP readiness for MODERATE often aligns with a 6–9 month program if you require vendor attestation and evidence collection concurrently.

If Acme shares their target audit window, we can produce a sequenced plan with checkboxes and owners.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sally Park <sally.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evidence ask + sequencing question for FedRAMP/ISO

Karthik / team — this is helpful, thank you.

BlueBank (copied) is targeting a MODERATE authorization path and wants to see the phased plan and the matrix by EOW next Friday (2026-10-09). They also asked for a short note about any compensating controls you expect to propose for gaps tied to third-party telemetry.

Can you confirm on timeline: matrix + sequenced roadmap by 10/09, and a follow-up 30-minute call to review on 10/12? If you can edit the Drive folder you listed, we'll drop the auditor contact preferences there.

Best,
Sally Park
Director, InfoSec - Acme Corp
